clue.text: Note or two notes

definitions.meaning: renown or distinction, as in 'a writer of note'
FA and ME are the fourth and third notes of the tonic sol-fa scale, side by side

explanation.surface: A puzzle about music theory: is it one note or a pair?
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is really a tiny charade: FA plus ME (a spelling of mi) from the sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of note means being well known, so note is a synonym for celebrity or renown.

clue.text: Worries and a lot of fear with this sharp blade

parts.note: to worry is to fret, so worries gives frets

indicators.note: most of the word, not all, so its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A nervous craftsman eyes a dangerous cutting tool with dread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims AWE to AW.
explanation.definitionFit: A fretsaw is a fine-bladed saw used to cut intricate curves in wood.

clue.text: Source of igneous rock featured in two publications (one not good)

indicators.note: one of the two copies is 'not good', so it loses the letter for good
the word two asks for the magazine abbreviation to appear twice in a row

parts.note: MAG is short for magazine, a publication

explanation.surface: A geology article appears in two magazines, one of them poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two' doubles MAG; 'one not' takes the G off the second copy, leaving MAG + MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten rock below the surface cools and solidifies into igneous rock such as granite and basalt.

clue.text: MC's twin interrupted by staff

indicators.note: the word for twin is broken into by the staff, which sits in the middle

parts.note: a ringer is a dead ringer, someone's exact double
a mast is a pole or staff

explanation.surface: A master of ceremonies has an identical twin who gets cut off by a member of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees, but it is a pole. The 's after MC stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus ringmaster announces the acts, acting as master of ceremonies for the show.

clue.text: Uncouth, upsetting me all dinner

indicators.note: upsetting knocks the letters over into a new order

explanation.surface: A boorish guest spoils the whole dinner party for me.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone rude and lacking social graces.

clue.text: Show — show up or show down, as it were

indicators.text: up or show down, as it were
indicators.note: in a down entry the word can be written upwards or downwards and still read the same

explanation.surface: A playful riddle about a show turning up or failing.
explanation.walkthrough: GIG is a palindrome, so in a down light it reads the same whether written up or down.
explanation.definitionFit: A gig is a live performance by musicians or comedians, a kind of show.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory local 24 25

definitions.meaning: a local is a neighbourhood pub, and one without beer is a poor one
an Australian song, the answers at 24 and 25 read together

explanation.surface: A disappointing neighbourhood bar and a tune from Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Pub With No Beer' is a 1950s Australian country song made famous by Slim Dusty. In Britain a 'local' is the pub nearest one's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a bar that has run dry, and also the title of a well-known Australian country song.

clue.text: Cover for religious figure in train, possibly

indicators.note: the saint's name is placed inside the rearranged letters
possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: Paul is the apostle Saint Paul

explanation.surface: A saint travelling by rail needs some kind of cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' scrambles the rail word into TARIN, and 'in' places the apostle after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a heavy waterproof sheet stretched over things to protect them.

clue.text: Came up around ship on a cold body of water

indicators.note: the word for came up is placed around the ship

parts.note: rose means ascended or came up

explanation.surface: A ship surfaces in a freezing sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' splits the verb after its second letter so the ship abbreviation sits in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ross Sea is a deep bay of the Southern Ocean off Antarctica, icy and frigid.

clue.text: Accepting bit of research, somehow I grew mature NZ grape variety

indicators.note: the jumbled letters accept, or take in, one more letter
somehow says the letters come together in some other order
a bit of the word, its first letter

explanation.surface: A New Zealand wine researcher grew vines to maturity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' scrambles I GREW MATURE NZ; 'Accepting' takes in R, the first letter of research, given by 'bit of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gewurztraminer is an aromatic white wine grape, grown in Alsace, Germany and New Zealand.

clue.text: Keen-sighted figure keen to embrace Left, not Right

indicators.note: not removes the letter for right
the word for keen holds the letter for left within it

explanation.surface: A political observer, eager to embrace the Left rather than the Right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to embrace' puts L inside EAGER, giving EAGLER; 'not' takes the R away.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagles are famed for very sharp eyesight, and the bird is a common emblem or figure.

clue.text: Pool attendants not provided, but receiving extra good protection for members

indicators.note: the shortened word receives one more letter added inside
not takes away the word for provided

parts.note: lifeguards watch over swimmers at a pool
if means provided, as in 'provided that'

explanation.surface: No lifeguards at the pool, yet swimmers are kept safe some other way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' leaves LEGUARDS. In cricket, leg guards are the batter's pads.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbs are members, so pads strapped on to shield the legs protect members.

clue.text: Small woman clutching end of that kitchen utensil

indicators.note: the woman's name holds the letter inside it
the final letter of the word that

explanation.surface: A petite woman grips a kitchen tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' gives T; 'clutching' puts it inside PAULA, giving PATULA.
explanation.definitionFit: A spatula is a flat, flexible blade used in cooking for lifting or spreading.

clue.text: Things to be avoided by feet intimidate old man on way back

definitions.text: Things to be avoided by feet

parts.note: to cow someone is to intimidate them
pa is a familiar word for father, one's old man

indicators.note: back says the street abbreviation is turned around

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone bullies an elderly man on the way home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ST into TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Walkers in fields watch their step to keep from treading in cattle dung.

clue.text: Roughly nothing in disastrous meal-time is herbal drink

parts.note: CA is short for circa, meaning roughly

indicators.note: the zero goes inside the jumbled letters
disastrous says the letters have gone wrong and are muddled

explanation.surface: A dinner disaster leaves almost nothing to eat but a soothing brew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disastrous' rearranges MEALTIME to MMILETEA; 'in' slips O in after the first M.
explanation.definitionFit: Camomile tea is an infusion of camomile flowers, a classic herbal tisane.

clue.text: Energy in Disney musical based on Dahl providing 24 25

indicators.note: the energy goes in between the two names

parts.note: Matilda is a stage musical from Roald Dahl's novel

explanation.surface: Mixing Disney's energy with a Roald Dahl musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disney musical' tempts as one show, but Disney is the first name alone and the Dahl musical is separate; 'in' sets the energy between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Waltzing Matilda is the best-known Australian folk song, often called the unofficial national anthem.

clue.text: University dance held up in stories implying no exciting music

indicators.note: the university and dance go inside the word for stories
in a down entry, held up means written upwards, so the dance is reversed

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A university dance is postponed amid rumours of dull music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' reverses only the dance, and 'in' places the result after the first letter of the stories word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lullabies are gentle songs meant to soothe a child to sleep, the opposite of rousing.

clue.text: Scruffy coal miner, person producing eruption from star

indicators.note: scruffy suggests something untidy, so the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: An unkempt coal miner turns out to be the source of an outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: A solar prominence is a huge loop of glowing gas erupting from the Sun's surface.

clue.text: A lot of hard work to secure answer for city

indicators.note: the shortened word holds the abbreviation fast inside it
most of the word, so its last letter goes

explanation.surface: It takes a lot of graft to get an answer for the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' drops the last letter of the toil word, leaving SWEA, and 'to secure' wraps it round the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a coastal city in south Wales.

clue.text: Each listener catches standard British speech — though not with this!

indicators.note: the two pieces catch, or trap, the speech abbreviation between them

parts.note: lug is slang for an ear, a listener
RP is Received Pronunciation, the standard accent of British English

explanation.surface: Every listener picks up proper British English, unless something blocks their ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catches' sets the accent abbreviation between the first two pieces. The definition is the clue's punchline: with this in, you would hear no speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wearing a plug in the ear canal would not catch speech, which the clue's punchline points to.

clue.text: Worried article gets harmed when taken across river

indicators.note: the injured word is stretched across, or around, the river letter

explanation.surface: An item is damaged while being carried over a river, and someone is fretful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when taken across' puts R inside LAMED, giving LARMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarmed and worried both describe someone anxious or frightened.

clue.text: Skies opening, disgorging a crustacean

parts.note: to sky a ball is to hit it high, to lob it

indicators.note: disgorging means throwing out, so the letter a is removed

parts.note: a tear is a rip, an opening

explanation.surface: The heavens open and the sea throws up a shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skies' looks like a noun but is a verb: hitting high. 'disgorging' takes A out of TEAR, leaving TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobster is a large marine crustacean with big claws.

clue.text: Dry up over augmented motor

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Something dries up after a car engine is boosted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns BRUT to TURB.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbocharged engine has its power boosted by a turbine forcing in extra air.

clue.text: One occupying second family home that's least substantial

indicators.note: the numeral one occupies, or lives in, the other pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone lives in the family's second home, which is the flimsiest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying' puts I inside NEST, giving NIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The thinnest thing has the least substance or bulk.

clue.text: Be emotional after beheading fish

indicators.note: beheading cuts off the head, the word's first letter

parts.note: to feel is to experience emotion

explanation.surface: Someone grows tearful after cutting the head off a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long snake-like fish.

clue.text: Name of 24 actor filling another role

indicators.note: the name fills the middle of these words, hidden across their join

explanation.surface: An actor from Down Under takes on a different part.
explanation.walkthrough: Errol Flynn, the swashbuckling film star, was born in Tasmania; 24 is AUSTRALIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Errol is the first name of Flynn, the Tasmanian-born Hollywood star.

clue.text: Articles about American trial upset someone from another country

indicators.note: the two articles go about, or around, the rest

parts.note: a and an are the indefinite articles

indicators.note: upset says the letters are overturned and rearranged

explanation.surface: Newspaper pieces about an American court case upset a foreigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the court word into TRALI, and 'about' has one article at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian is a native of Australia, a country other than the one the solver is in.

clue.text: Very much needing evacuated air

parts.note: so means very much, as in 'so kind'

indicators.note: evacuated means emptied, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone badly needs to get out into the fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' looks like the atmosphere; it is a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a melody or tune, so it is a synonym for a piece of music sung.
